messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT created — hosted-api us-east-1 queue growth. p95 and p99 spike, many requests timing out. Auto-scaler reports failed allocations.

olivia-oncall: I'm paged, joining. seeing 6x baseline qlen on host-queues, p99 ~ 12s. pulling metrics now.

raj-sre: on my way. any recent deploys?

olivia-oncall: no deploys in last 3 hours. traffic spike looks organic, started ~ 10m ago.

casey-infra: provisioning errors from cloud provider for GPU nodes: "Insufficient capacity" across two AZs. autoscaler kept retrying and hit API quota.

olivia-oncall: ok — current mitigation attempt: enable fallback routing to smaller model (gpt-small-quant) for non-SLAs. Will flip ramp to 30% and monitor.

maya-support: support queue filling — several customers reporting 504s. tagging customers with high usage to outbound.

raj-sre: quick check — eviction logs show a thrash between thinpool and default pools. suspect provisioner rate-limit and leader election delays.

casey-infra: confirmed. provisioner requests are being rate-limited by cloud quota; we can request immediate quota emergency but that takes ops handoff. short-term: enable edge-provisioner fallback (thin warm nodes) and relax eviction thresholds.

olivia-oncall: doing two things now: 1) enable fallback routing (30% -> 70% over 5m); 2) lower batch size for high-latency models to reduce per-token queue time.

raj-sre: please post the exact commands you run.

olivia-oncall: running: ```
# enable fallback route
redwoodctl route set-hosted --region us-east-1 --policy fallback --variant gpt-small-quant --weight 30
# temp throttle for noisy tenants
redwoodctl tenant throttle --ids T-1234,T-9988 --rate 20r/s
```

casey-infra: enabling thin warm nodes now. ETA ~ 4m. also contacting cloud partner for immediate quota bump.

maya-support: messaging update to affected customers: "We're experiencing elevated latency in us-east-1; we're routing traffic to lower-cost model variants while we restore capacity. Some requests may be rate-limited. We'll update in 15m."

leo-product: any customer-visible SLO breaches yet? need list of impacted tenant IDs for legal/comms.

maya-support: gathering tenant list from logs, posting in #support-ops shortly. so far 12 tenants with >5% error increase.

raj-sre: telemetry — p95 dropped from 12s -> 3.8s after fallbacks enabled; p99 still ~9s but trending down. queue length halved. autoscaler still failing to create full-sized GPU nodes.

olivia-oncall: keeping an eye on the provisioner heartbeats. If thin warm nodes are up we should be able to gracefully move more weight to higher-capacity backends next 10m.

casey-infra: thin warm nodes are up (3 instances). starting traffic shift: bump weight to 55%.

olivia-oncall: bumped. observing errors on a single tenant that pin memory on model servers — applying tenant-specific throttle.

maya-support: posted tenant list to #support-ops and emailed account teams for top 3.

raj-sre: request: open incident ticket for cloud quota with infra escalation. this looks like capacity shortage rather than software bug.

casey-infra: ticket opened with cloud partner ID 0-ABCD-Emergency. also temporarily relaxing quota enforcer for provisioner to allow retries every 10s.

olivia-oncall: monitoring: p99 down to 4.7s, overall error rate normalized to baseline +1.5%. stack traces show timeouts decreased after fallback.

leo-product: good call on fallback. can we capture timeline and decisions for postmortem?

olivia-oncall: noted. will annotate steps in timeline.

maya-support: confirming customers updated. one high-tier customer requested immediate SLA credit eval. forwarding to sales/finance.

raj-sre: handoff — I'm taking on-call for the next hour to oversee scale and cloud ticket. olivia, please hand any follow-ups to me.

olivia-oncall: handing off to @raj-sre — summary: provisioner hit cloud capacity/quota limits, enabled fallback routing and thin warm nodes, p99 reduced, error rates nearly back to normal.

incident-bot: INCIDENT status -> mitigated. active mitigations: fallback routing, thin-warm pool, tenant throttles. next steps: continue monitoring, await cloud quota resolution, postmortem.

raj-sre: will keep thread updated. request all relevant logs uploaded to incident doc: /incidents/hosted-queue-1799995000. set follow-up for postmortem tomorrow 10:00 PT.

maya-support: mark customer comms follow-up done.

olivia-oncall: thanks team — will add runbook executions and exact command outputs to the incident doc. :white_check_mark:

raj-sre: closing paging for now, keeping watch. please react with :thumbsup: when you acknowledge the handoff.

maya-support: :thumbsup:

casey-infra: :thumbsup:

leo-product: :thumbsup:

incident-bot: INCIDENT closed -> monitoring.
